I choose sponsors for five or six events every year, and I always ask three questions. First: is this company a good fit for our members? A sponsor has to be interesting for the people in the room. Second: what does the sponsor want in return? The biggest offer is not always the best one, because some sponsors ask for too much. For example, a long presentation in the middle of a breakfast. And third: is the company reliable? In my experience, a reliable sponsor that pays on time is more valuable than a famous sponsor that pays three months late. So I do not only compare the numbers. I compare the whole package.

A few years ago, our company sponsored big international conferences. They were famous, and we had a lot of visibility. But they were also very expensive, and honestly, not very effective. We met hundreds of people, but very few of them became partners. Now we sponsor smaller events at a chamber of commerce. The package is more affordable, and the events are much more cost-effective for us. The best benefit is direct contact with the people who make decisions in the member companies. It is not as glamorous as a big conference, but the results are better.
